description:
LANDED 5a1ba823b on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Research with
prototype, cold review (approve-with-fixes; eight fixes folded, one of them a
red gate), rebased onto fz-kdt.193.

THIS IS UNSOUNDNESS, NOT PRECISION, and the witness is on the corpus. At base
00277_enum_tier0_fixture publishes `main/0[] return fp[L] list(:tail)` and
keys `Kernel.dbg/1[fp[L] list(:tail)]` while the program prints
`[7, 5, 3, 1, :tail]`. The published type does not contain the value, and an
executable is keyed on it -- the fz-kdt.132/138 class. Here it publishes
`list(int | :tail)` and mints the distinct
`Enum.reduce_finish/1[{:done, list(int | :tail)}]`, which is the +1
executable.

THE RULE: a @spec variable's lower bound is the JOIN of its covariant
occurrences, and a join needs every term. Where the walk reaches an occurrence
it cannot read -- the witness carries vars, or names no structure of the
pattern's kind, so every collector answers MatchWitness::Unknown -- that term
is UNKNOWN, not `none`. What Sigma holds is then a PARTIAL join, and since
`Known` claims a runtime fact, a result naming a partially-joined variable
answers Underconstrained. MatchBounds gains `undetermined`;
collect_match_subst is the one marking site; collect_lower_occurrences mirrors
the collectors and reuses fz-kdt.184's BindingSide::flipped().

STATED AS IMPLEMENTED, NOT AS IDEALISED: the marking fires on a node's MERGED
outcome, so what the rule delivers is "no node the walk visited was wholly
unreadable", not "every covariant occurrence was individually read". Two
collectors skip a single occurrence while a sibling keeps the node Known --
collect_map_match's absent key and collect_arrow_match's arity-incompatible
clause. Both are pinned KNOWN-WRONG with the reason (neither is reachable from
the shipped library, which declares no map-typed and no multi-clause @spec),
and fz-kdt.218 owns closing them correct-by-construction. The docs say the
implemented rule, not the stronger one.

WHY THE COST IS ACCEPTABLE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED: 1,189 verdicts stop
claiming a fact (match_arrow K 20,807 -> 19,618, U 2,952 -> 4,215, I 14,286 ->
14,326). At the consumer those produce ABSENT +447 and NOOP -817 -- they were
doing nothing -- and the only four that were doing anything are the four
CARVEs this fixes. That measurement is recorded in the code so a later reader
does not "optimise" per-node marking into per-occurrence marking. FILL, the
useful narrowing, is untouched (354 -> 357 under the review's classifier).

THE DEFECT IS LIVE WITH THE CLEANER INTACT, which is what makes this a bug in
its own right rather than only a fz-kdt.120 prerequisite: a census of every
refine_call_return invocation over 605 fixtures finds EIGHT CARVE events (a
constrained observed return narrowed to a strict subset), every one at site 1
analyze_activation, every one this defect -- `{:done, [int | :tail]}` ->
`{:done, [:tail]}` on 00277, `{:done, int|float}` -> `{:done, int}` on
mailbox_closure_enum_hofs and map_enumerable, `{:done, {:acc,{int|float,any}}}`
-> `{:done, {:acc,{int,any}}}` on enum_tier0 and fz_f98_map_reduce, and
`{:done, any}` -> `{:done, int}` on mailbox_closure_reduce. The count is 0
here. The fz-f98.16 empty-list cleaner masks only the `[]` instance.

TWO DEFERRED FIXTURES ARE REVIVED. enum_tier0 and fz_f98_map_reduce carried
six defer.{build,interp,run} lines naming fz-bfh.3; both now match their
PRE-EXISTING expected.txt byte-for-byte on interp, run and build (those
goldens were last touched in d5438ba08 and are untouched here), and their
stale "why this is deferred" prose is rewritten to current fact. The matrix
goes 509 passed / 9 ignored -> 515 passed / 3 ignored.

THE RED GATE THE REVIEW FOUND, AND HOW IT WAS RESOLVED WITHOUT BAKING IN A
KNOWN DEFECT: reviving enum_tier0 made matrix::enum_tier0::run exceed its 3 s
default (measured 3.13 / 3.60 / 3.85 s; the clock starts at execution-ready
and the fixture JIT-lowers 259 executables where base lowered 70), so the
prototype was 514/1/3. fixture_matrix builds a door's timeout only from a
`timeout.<door>_secs` directive, one door per line, so the raise needs a line
-- and adding one shifts the fixture's leading-comment count, which
normalize_gutter_line_ref subtracts from a gutter rendered out of
runtime:Enum.fz (fz-kdt.19). The line was added and a prose line compressed to
hold the frontmatter count steady, with all new explanatory prose placed below
the blank line where leading_comment_lines has already stopped. Neither
expected.txt was regenerated. The fixture header records the constraint and
names fz-kdt.19.

DIVERGENCES FROM THE REVIEW, EACH DELIBERATE AND STATED: fix 6 was taken as a
correctness improvement instead of a deletion -- collect_lower_occurrences'
memo is now keyed on the whole BindingSide (which gained Hash) rather than on
`side == Lower`, so no two sides share a slot and the Unify arm needs no
invariant to stay safe. Two reviewer probes were RESHAPED because as written
they do not isolate the property they claim: P3 answers Underconstrained at
base and head via has_vars(param), and P7 likewise via has_vars(result); each
was given a declared bound so the marking, and the `!sigma.contains_key`
exception, are what the pin observes. P8 was dropped (its invariant is not
load-bearing after the memo fix) and P9 as a duplicate. Three review claims
were stale and no duplicate tickets were filed for them: fz-kdt.216 already
owns the parameter-half false spec/violation, and fz-kdt.19 already owns the
gutter normaliser.

MEASURED (605 fixtures / 476 dumps, against dd07432db, both binaries run
against the same sources; stdout+stderr normalised for thread id, backtrace
addresses and the embedded worktree path per fz-kdt.211): interp 2 movers and
run 2 movers, both being the two revived fixtures (base died
`fz panic: "Enum.EmptyError"`); canon 6 movers, exactly the six fixtures that
CARVE; executables 5,548 -> 5,755, of which enum_tier0 is 70 -> 259,
fz_f98_map_reduce 34 -> 51 and 00277 177 -> 178, EVERY OTHER FIXTURE
IDENTICAL; FIFO/LIFO 2 movers both ways at base and here, with the two revived
fixtures canon-identical under both schedules; lib 1,709/0/5 -> 1,720/0/5;
matrix 515/0/3. A lane cost is recorded rather than hidden:
Enum.reduce/3[non_empty_list(int), int, any] in behavior/mailbox_closure_reduce
moves from `return fp[int] int` with reprs=[RawInt] to `return fp[any] any`
with reprs=[ValueRef].

fz-kdt.120 IS NOW A PURE DELETION, measured by stacking its cleaner removal on
top of this and then reverting: interp and run each move only the two fixtures
this ticket fixes, the seven previously-regressing fixtures are byte-identical
to base on both doors, executables stay at 5,755, dbg([]) publishes
empty_list() instead of any, Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as list(int), and
FIFO/LIFO canon movers go to ZERO -- both schedule-dependent fixtures
converge. That leaves 120 as a 147-line deletion plus its own re-pins.

RESIDUES, EACH OWNED: fz-kdt.218 (the two latent per-node marking holes);
fz-kdt.216 (the PARAMETER half of the same root -- refine_contract_inputs
clamping a reducer's arrow to the seed accumulator, a false spec/violation at
base and here); fz-kdt.19 (the gutter normaliser this had to work around);
fz-kdt.190 is neither re-broken nor subsumed -- its stated instance no longer
reproduces at this head, its half (a) improves as CARVE goes 8 -> 0, and its
half (b) survives at CARVE_EMPTY_KEEP 13 -> 9.

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded commit, rebased onto fz-kdt.193 (marker COORD-GATE-1788479779): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1720 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored, fixture matrix single-threaded 515 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored -- six previously-ignored trials now run.
title: A ground seed argument instantiates a @spec return variable and refine_call_return MEETS it into the published return: reduce_cont keyed on list(int) publishes {:done, []}
